target.title: fix(cli): warn that attach --print-config prints a live bearer token
target.body:
Closes #104517

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where `openclaw attach --print-config` prints the full MCP
grant config, including `env.OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN` (a live, unrevoked bearer
credential), as plain JSON on stdout with no indication that it is sensitive.
A user copying that output into a log, chat transcript, screen share, or bug
report can leak the live token without realizing it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a clear warning printed to stderr immediately before the JSON payload is
printed to stdout. This keeps the warning visible to interactive users while
staying separable from stdout for any scripted consumers that pipe/parse the
JSON. This is the minimal fix addressing the issue's first suggested option
(a clear warning) without changing the printed config shape, redacting the
token (which would break the documented copy/launch workflow), or making a
larger product decision about a separate summary/redact mode.

## User Impact

Anyone running `attach --print-config` now sees an explicit stderr warning
that the printed env carries a live bearer token and should be treated as a
secret, reducing accidental credential leakage via copy/paste or logging.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test asserting an `ERR:`-prefixed stderr warning
  containing `OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN` and `secret` is emitted, and that it appears
  before the JSON payload in output order.
- Proved the regression: temporarily removed the new warning call and reran
  the test, which failed on the missing stderr assertion. Restored the fix
  and confirmed the test passes again.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts` — 12/12 passed.
- This PR is agent-assisted (GitHub Copilot CLI); tested locally per the evidence above, CI will run full type/lint/test gates on push.
